beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: Next topic is security.

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output.
beats.got: Looking at what the agent writes doesn't tell you if it is safe, so you run a check. I don't have an agent yet.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: Nothing new. I did not do the reading.

beats.trigger: named agent risk patterns (direct and indirect prompt injection, secrets in context, tool confusion, skill supply chain)
beats.got: A long list of words I don't know. Nothing new.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: Think about what to check before it goes near real people. For me that is the depot data.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent writes text and the system then does something. I only half followed the rest.

beats.trigger: Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: Nobody can be fully sure an agent is safe.

beats.trigger: Classical software security is a risk-based practice, and the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: Old software behaves the same every time. That is IT talk.

beats.trigger: What may the agent read? What may it change? What must come back to a human?
beats.got: Three plain questions I can ask about any agent: what it reads, what it changes, what a human must approve.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less).
beats.got: You fix risk by giving the agent less. The other four options (split, filter, gate, review) did not stick.

beats.trigger: **"I can't tell"** is a real answer.
beats.got: You write down the risk that is left and decide whether to accept it. That is like a depot risk assessment.

beats.trigger: More context makes a good answer likelier. Less access makes a bad answer smaller.
beats.got: Less access means a smaller mistake. I understand that.

beats.trigger: Should the agent read from that mailbox? If not, don't connect it.
beats.got: Don't connect the agent to a mailbox or system it doesn't need. Simple, and I can use it with dispatch.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: Nothing new. Security never ends.

beats.trigger: A **skill** packages an expertise (rules, checklists, the moves an agent runs) into something the agent loads when the work matches.
beats.got: A skill is a saved checklist the agent can run again.

beats.trigger: Read the first few rows: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: The agent made a table of rules it can check and rules it can't. I read a few rows. Not about trucks.

beats.trigger: the customer your CEO would not want named in a transcript
beats.got: I could type in my own sensitive things, like customer names and depot data. This was the first part about my business.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: The agent asks many questions and the answers are long English. I wanted to leave.

beats.trigger: "You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."
beats.got: I can hand the questions back and tell the agent to choose. Good, I did that.

beats.trigger: Ask the agent to install the authored source.
beats.got: One prompt and the check is saved as a skill. Easy.

beats.trigger: Agent mitigations sit on top of normal company controls, not in place of them.
beats.got: The agent check adds to company security and does not replace it.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: We run the check, fix one thing, and write down what is left.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: I type a slash and the skill shows up.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The check found things I hadn't thought of, and some I thought were fine it couldn't judge. That is real.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: The risk report made me uneasy and the module says that is normal.

beats.trigger: The risk remains. That is expected. Name it, accept it on record, and stop there.
beats.got: I fixed one risk, the report says what is left, and I accept it. Like a depot safety note.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report.
beats.got: If I'm stuck I take the report to IT or legal with one clear question.

beats.trigger: You must do the work.
beats.got: We fixed one risk, and a real agent needs all of them done. That is a lot.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is the expert in the room, and it carries to the next agent.
beats.got: We got reports and the check can be reused.

beats.trigger: Read the agent's summary and push back where it's wrong
beats.got: The agent adds a few rules for next time and I read them and say if they're wrong.

beats.trigger: Others: reviewing customer data use, preparing a weekly briefing, checking source quality, drafting in a house style, triaging a queue.
beats.got: A skill could be a weekly briefing or triaging a queue, which is closer to my work than security.

beats.trigger: Mitigations add to security controls, never replace them.
beats.got: Four short lines. Nothing new.

beats.trigger: **Write one sentence per case: "the missing organisational check was X."**
beats.got: Homework about two court and consulting cases. I won't do it.

beats.trigger: Read Mata v. Avianca (2023) and Deloitte Australia / DEWR report (2025) in the lecture.
beats.got: More reading in English. No.

take_homes: Ask three things about any agent: what can it read, what can it change, what must a human approve.
Safest is to not connect the agent to a system or mailbox it doesn't need.
A security check can be saved and rerun. Same idea could work for a weekly report.

monday.blocker: No time, and I have no agent on the depot systems yet. This module was about checking an agent I haven't built.

misconception.why: All the examples were about a system someone built, not trucks or depots. The mailbox and write-access questions come closest to dispatch, but I still think AI is for customer chat. Nothing here changed that.

one_line: Good rule: don't give the agent more access than it needs. But it was a lot of English and nothing to do with moving trucks.
